title: Why Does Starch Turn Blue? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
One drop of iodine turns a potato slice blue-black, but a ball of cotton stays the same, even though both are built from glucose. Aarav asks: why the difference? And how does a sugar chain hold a colour?

We build a polysaccharide sugar by sugar, zoom from a plant cell wall to a cellulose chain to one glucose ring, meet cellulose, starch, glycogen, inulin and chitin step by step, and watch the iodine test happen inside the starch helix. Then the parts of a nucleotide, nucleoside vs nucleotide, purines and pyrimidines, DNA vs RNA with a pause and think, a worked example naming molecules from their building blocks, the nucleoside exam trap, an original NEET assertion-reason question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 71 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:
0:00 Potato, cotton and iodine
0:36 What is a polysaccharide?
0:58 Zoom ladder: cell wall, cellulose, glucose
1:19 Five polysaccharides
1:57 The iodine test
2:14 Nucleotides: three parts
2:37 Purines, pyrimidines, DNA and RNA + pause and think
3:07 Worked example: name it from its building block
3:29 Exam trap: nucleoside or nucleotide?
3:49 Practice question (NEET pattern)
4:13 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Structure of Proteins. How does a straight chain of amino acids fold into a working machine?
